title: A protocol for human bone marrow adipocyte isolation and purification
protocol: Expose the intramedullary canal during femur preparation, especially in young patients using a first broach if necessary.
Aspirate bone marrow cautiously from the femoral proximal metaphysis and diaphysis with a 60 ml syringe and soft cannula.
Place aspirated bone marrow (10–20 ml) immediately into a pre-warmed tube containing 20 ml KRBHA at 37°C.
Transfer the tube to a transport bag for rapid delivery to the laboratory within 1 hour.
Wash and collect bone marrow samples.
Rinse the cell strainer with KRBHA.
Pour the tissue on the rinsed cell strainer.
Wash the tissue with 20 mL warm KRBHA.
Transfer the BM sample to a petri dish.
Dissect the yellow BM-AT using tweezers and scissors.
Weigh the dissected BM-AT prior to isolation.
Place a 100 μm cell strainer on top of a 50 mL tube.
Rinse the strainer with KRBHA.
Pour the tissue sample onto the strainer.
Add 20 mL KRBHA to the sample to remove blood.
Collect the BM sample present on the strainer using tweezers.
Transfer the collected BM sample to a petri dish.
Isolate only the areas of BM-AT recognized by their yellow color.
Add 10 mL KRBHA to the petri dish to wash the BM-AT.
Transfer BM-AT to a pre-weighed 14 mL tube.
Weigh the tube containing BM-AT and calculate the tissue weight.
Use 2.5 mL collagenase 1× solution per gram of tissue.
Calculate the volume of collagenase 1× solution necessary for the experiment.
Prepare the collagenase 1× solution by diluting the 5× stock solution in PBS 2% BSA.
Add the collagenase 1× solution to the tube containing the BM-AT.
Close the tube and seal it with parafilm.
Place the tube in a horizontal position on an orbital shaker at 37°C, 150 rpm.
Incubate for roughly 20 min.
Filter the suspension through a 100 μm cell strainer.
Rinse the strainer with warm KRBHA.
Wait a few minutes to allow adipocytes to float at the surface.
Remove a maximum of KRBHA to facilitate adipocyte collection.
Transfer BM-Ads with a 1 mL pipet to a new 2 mL tube.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 g at 22°C to pellet contaminant cells.
Check the digestion regularly from 15 minutes onwards.
Place a 100 μm cell strainer on top of a 50 mL tube and rinse the strainer with KRBHA.
Filter the suspension through the strainer to remove cellular debris, undigested fragments, and bone trabeculae.
Pour 20 mL KRBHA onto the strainer to recover BM-Ads.
Wait 1–3 minutes for lipid-laden adipocytes to rise up and float at the surface.
Remove 15–18 mL of KRBHA from under floating BM-Ads with a syringe and a 21G needle.
Collect gently floating BM-Ads with a 1 mL pipette using standard P1000 pipette tip.
Transfer collected adipocytes to a 2 mL tube.
Rinse the cell strainer and pipette tips with KRBHA before pouring or pipetting adipocytes.
Add 1 mL of KRBHA to the suspension and mix gently by tilting.
Wait until adipocytes rise again to form an upper layer, KRBHA being in the lower layer.
Aspirate the KRBHA using a 2 mL syringe with a 21G needle and discard it.
Add 1 mL of KRBHA and wait until adipocytes rise again to form an upper layer.
Centrifuge for 5 min at 200 g, 22°C.
Transfer floating adipocytes to a new tube.
Wash and centrifuge BM-Ads.
Note: Pipette adipocytes gently during preparation to limit lysis.
Prepare adipocyte cell suspension as quickly as possible after isolation.
For molecular analyses, freeze known volumes of isolated adipocytes in liquid nitrogen and store them at -80°C.
Wash cells twice with PBS before freezing for Western blotting.
Mix BM-Ads with fibrinogen.
Dilute thrombin with PBS containing 2 mM CaCl2.
Gently mix 30 μL adipocytes with 30 μL fibrinogen.
Add 30 μL diluted thrombin and mix until gel polymerizes.
Avoid forming bubbles during mixing.
Keep the gel for 2 minutes at 20°C–25°C.
Under a chemical hood, add 400 μL 3.7% PFA to the gel.
Incubate with PFA on an orbital shaker at 100 rpm for 20 minutes.
Remove PFA and wash the gel twice with PBS.
Add staining solution containing BODIPY 493/503, rhodamine-coupled phalloidin, and TO-PRO3 iodide diluted in PBS to the gel.
Incubate on an orbital shaker at 100 rpm for 1 hour while protecting from light.
Remove staining solution and wash the gel twice with PBS.
Reconstitute BODIPY 493/503 stock solution in DMSO or ethanol at a concentration of 1 μg/mL.
Aliquot the reconstituted BODIPY 493/503 solution in dark tubes and store at -20°C for several months.
Prepare TO-PRO3 iodide 642/661 as recommended by the supplier, avoiding freeze-thawing cycles.
Make small aliquots of up to 10 μL of TO-PRO3 iodide and store them in dark tubes.
Dissolve PBS containing 3% BSA and 0.1% Triton ×100 for non-specific antigen saturation.
Incubate the gel with the saturation solution at 20°C–25°C for 1–2 hours.
Dilute primary antibodies in PBS containing 3% BSA and 0.1% Triton ×100 as determined by the user.
Stain the gel with diluted primary antibodies overnight at 4°C.
Wash the gel five times with PBS containing 0.05% Tween20 for 10 minutes each.
Incubate the gel with secondary antibodies in PBS containing 3% BSA and 0.1% Triton ×100 at 20°C–25°C for 2 hours.
Wash the gel five times with PBS containing 0.05% Tween20 for 10 minutes each.
Perform all incubations on an orbital shaking device at 100 rpm or a rotative shaker at 20 rpm.
Use alternative dyes such as DAPI or Hoechst33342 to stain nuclei if UV or blue laser light is available on the imaging system.
Handle the gel carefully with a curved clamp and place it on a 150 μm coverslip for imaging.
Put the coverslip on an inverted confocal microscope.
Set up confocal light path with correct excitation and emission wavelengths according to the dyes used for staining.
Excite BODIPY 493/503 stained lipids with a 488 nm blue laser.
Collect emission signals from BODIPY 493/503 at 510 ± 15 nm.
Excite rhodamine-coupled phalloidin stained actin cytoskeleton with a 532 nm green laser.
Collect emission signals from phalloidin at 550 ± 15 nm.
Excite TO-PRO3 iodide 642/661 stained nuclei with a 635 nm red laser.
Collect emission signals from TO-PRO3 around 660 ± 20 nm.
